title: Test score cutoff and college enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the automatic-admission cutoff running_var = 0.5.
- Why: Treatment (automatic admission eligibility) is assigned deterministically by crossing the known threshold. We can identify the local average treatment effect at the cutoff from the discontinuity in enrollment.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff: in absence of treatment, E[y | running_var] is continuous at 0.5.
  - No precise manipulation of running_var around 0.5.
  - Correct functional form locally: we use local linear (and check quadratic), with kernel weighting and bandwidth sensitivity.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load data, run sharp RDD with local linear (triangular kernel), and report estimates
# Robustness: polynomial order, bandwidths, kernels, placebo cutoff, and (optionally) rdrobust if available.

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s26_data.csv")

# 2) Helper: Local linear sharp RDD
rdd_fit <- function(data, cutoff = 0.5, h = 0.3, poly = 1, kernel = "triangular") {
  # Center running variable
  x_all <- data$running_var - cutoff
  in_bw <- abs(x_all) <= h
  x <- x_all[in_bw]
  y <- data$y[in_bw]
  treated <- as.numeric(data$running_var[in_bw] >= cutoff)
  
  # Build design
  dat <- data.frame(y = y, treated = treated, x = x)
  if (poly >= 2) dat$x2 <- x^2
  
  # Weights
  if (kernel == "triangular") {
    w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(x) / h)
  } else {
    # uniform kernel as default alternative
    w <- rep(1, length(x))
  }
  
  # Formula: different slopes on each side + jump at cutoff (treated)
  if (poly == 1) {
    form <- y ~ treated + x + treated:x
  } else {
    form <- y ~ treated + x + treated:x + x2 + treated:x2
  }
  
  fit <- lm(form, data = dat, weights = w)
  
  # Robust (HC1) standard errors if available
  use_robust <- requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)
  if (use_robust) {
    vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
    ct <- lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = vc)
    if (!("treated" %in% rownames(ct))) {
      stop("Coefficient 'treated' not found. Check model specification.")
    }
    est <- ct["treated", 1]; se <- ct["treated", 2]; tval <- ct["treated", 3]; pval <- ct["treated", 4]
  } else {
    sm <- summary(fit)
    rn <- rownames(sm$coefficients)
    idx <- which(rn == "treated")
    if (length(idx) != 1) stop("Coefficient 'treated' not found. Check model specification.")
    est <- sm$coefficients[idx, 1]; se <- sm$coefficients[idx, 2]; tval <- sm$coefficients[idx, 3]; pval <- sm$coefficients[idx, 4]
  }
  ci_low <- est - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- est + 1.96 * se
  
  list(est = est, se = se, t = tval, p = pval, ci = c(ci_low, ci_high),
       n = length(y), h = h, poly = poly, kernel = kernel)
}

# 3) Main specification: local linear, triangular kernel, bandwidth h = 0.3 (matches near_cutoff definition)
main <- rdd_fit(df, cutoff = 0.5, h = 0.3, poly = 1, kernel = "triangular")
cat("MAIN RDD (c=0.5, h=0.3, local linear, triangular):\n")
cat(sprintf("  N (within h): %d\n  Jump (treated): %.4f\n  SE: %.4f\n  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n  p-value: %.4g\n\n",
            main$n, main$est, main$se, main$ci[1], main$ci[2], main$p))

# 4) Robustness: polynomial order (quadratic), bandwidth sensitivity, kernel sensitivity
# 4a) Quadratic
quad <- rdd_fit(df, cutoff = 0.5, h = 0.3, poly = 2, kernel = "triangular")
cat("ROBUSTNESS - Quadratic (c=0.5, h=0.3, triangular):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Jump: %.4f  SE: %.4f  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]  p-value: %.4g\n\n",
            quad$est, quad$se, quad$ci[1], quad$ci[2], quad$p))

# 4b) Bandwidth sensitivity (triangular)
for (h in c(0.20, 0.25, 0.30)) {
  fit_h <- rdd_fit(df, cutoff = 0.5, h = h, poly = 1, kernel = "triangular")
  cat(sprintf("ROBUSTNESS - Bandwidth h=%.2f (triangular):  Jump=%.4f  SE=%.4f  95%% CI=[%.4f, %.4f]  p=%.4g  N=%d\n",
              h, fit_h$est, fit_h$se, fit_h$ci[1], fit_h$ci[2], fit_h$p, fit_h$n))
}
cat("\n")

# 4c) Kernel sensitivity (uniform, h=0.3)
uniform_fit <- rdd_fit(df, cutoff = 0.5, h = 0.3, poly = 1, kernel = "uniform")
cat("ROBUSTNESS - Kernel (uniform, h=0.3):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Jump: %.4f  SE: %.4f  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]  p-value: %.4g  N=%d\n\n",
            uniform_fit$est, uniform_fit$se, uniform_fit$ci[1], uniform_fit$ci[2], uniform_fit$p, uniform_fit$n))

# 5) Placebo cutoff at 0.6 (within support)
placebo <- rdd_fit(df, cutoff = 0.6, h = 0.3, poly = 1, kernel = "triangular")
cat("PLACEBO RDD (c=0.6, h=0.3, local linear, triangular):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Jump: %.4f  SE: %.4f  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]  p-value: %.4g  N=%d\n\n",
            placebo$est, placebo$se, placebo$ci[1], placebo$ci[2], placebo$p, placebo$n))

# 6) Optional: Data-driven bandwidth with rdrobust (if installed)
if (requireNamespace("rdrobust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("RDROBUST (data-driven bandwidths, triangular, p=1):\n")
  rd <- rdrobust::rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = 0.5, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
  print(rd)
  cat("\n")
} else {
  cat("Note: Package 'rdrobust' not installed; skipped data-driven bandwidth estimation.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Crossing the automatic-admission threshold should raise actual enrollment.
- Magnitude: A local jump around 0.10–0.20 in outcome units at the cutoff is plausible, reflecting a sizable increase in enrollment probability among marginal admits. Robustness checks should preserve sign and significance; placebo at 0.6 should be near zero and insignificant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — test score cutoff; continuity of running variable required; McCrary density test
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Scoring above cutoff significantly increases college enrollment
